title: Frobenius sewing and exact two-dimensional topological amplitudes

items.title: Semisimple closed two-dimensional TQFT data
items.design_state: Assigned reserved design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded on the owning A/B page.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and let $A=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{r}\mathbb C e_i$, with coordinatewise multiplication $e_i e_j=\delta_{ij}e_i$ and unit $1_A=\sum_{i=1}^{r}e_i$. Choose weights $w_i\in\mathbb C^\times$ and define $\epsilon(e_i)=w_i$ and $\Delta(e_i)=w_i^{-1}e_i\otimes e_i$. The Frobenius pairing $b(a,b)=\epsilon(ab)$ is diagonal in the basis $(e_i)$ with entries $w_i$; $\Delta$ is the inverse-pairing comultiplication. These maps define a finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra over $\mathbb C$.

A **closed oriented two-dimensional TQFT** here is a strong symmetric monoidal functor from $\mathsf{Cob}^{\mathrm{cl}}_2$ to $\mathrm{Vect}_{\mathrm{fd}}(\mathbb C)$. The objects of $\mathsf{Cob}^{\mathrm{cl}}_2$ are finite ordered words of oriented circles; its morphisms are compact oriented smooth surfaces with parametrized incoming and outgoing circle boundaries and no free boundary, modulo orientation-preserving diffeomorphism relative to those boundary parameterizations. Composition is collar gluing and the monoidal operation is ordered disjoint union. The supplied closed classification associates to $(A,\mu,\eta,\Delta,\epsilon)$ a closed oriented two-dimensional TQFT. Put $H=\mu\circ\Delta$. For the connected closed surface $\Sigma_g$ of genus $g\ge0$, it assigns $Z_A(\Sigma_g)=\epsilon(H^g(\eta(1)))$; the cylinder acts by $1_A$.

This is a closed-sector construction. It asserts no open sector, Cardy datum, or fully extended point-level theory. Countable choice is inherited only through the root surface-normal-form input to the classification.

references.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories (short version)
Joachim Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D Topological Quantum Field Theories (Cambridge book excerpt)
Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3

items.strategy:
1.1 Coordinatewise multiplication is associative and commutative, and $1_A=\sum_i e_i$ is a unit because $e_i1_A=e_i$. The pairing matrix is $\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_r)$, whose determinant $\prod_i w_i$ is nonzero since every $w_i\ne0$; hence $b(a,b)=\epsilon(ab)$ is nondegenerate. [given, A1, algebra]

1.2 The formulas for $\Delta$ and $\epsilon$ are linear maps. For each $i$, both counit composites give $w_i^{-1}\epsilon(e_i)e_i=e_i$, and both coassociative composites give $w_i^{-2}e_i\otimes e_i\otimes e_i$. On a basis tensor $e_i\otimes e_j$, each of the two Frobenius composites and $\Delta\mu$ equals $0$ if $i\ne j$ and equals $w_i^{-1}e_i\otimes e_i$ if $i=j$. By bilinearity the counit, coassociativity, and Frobenius identities hold on all inputs, so these maps form a commutative Frobenius algebra. [given, A1, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F1] to the finite-dimensional commutative Frobenius algebra established in steps 1.1–1.2. The resulting functor has the genus-$g$ evaluation and cylinder action stated in the Definition by [F2]; no positivity or open-sector hypothesis is used. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Sewing diagram

The following typed composition displays the handle operator used by the classification: $\Delta$ splits one state into two tensor factors and $\mu$ joins those factors. The diagram records the map types and composition only; the algebraic identities and surface classification above establish the result independently of the drawing.

```tikzcd
A \arrow[r,"\Delta"] & A\otimes A \arrow[r,"\mu"] & A
```

items.title: Handle operators give explicit genus amplitudes
items.design_state: Assigned reserved design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded on the owning A/B page.
items.statement: For the semisimple closed model defined by the stated idempotent data, let $H=\mu\circ\Delta$ and let $g\ge0$ be an integer. The connected closed genus-$g$ amplitude is $Z_A(\Sigma_g)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i^{1-g}$. The cylinder acts by $1_A$, and the torus amplitude is $r$.

references.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories (short version)
Joachim Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D Topological Quantum Field Theories (Cambridge book excerpt)
Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3

items.strategy:
1.1 For every $i$, $H(e_i)=\mu(w_i^{-1}e_i\otimes e_i)=w_i^{-1}e_i$ because $e_i^2=e_i$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Since $\eta(1)=\sum_i e_i$, repeated application of the diagonal action in step 1.1 gives $H^g(\eta(1))=\sum_i w_i^{-g}e_i$ for each integer $g\ge0$; at $g=0$ this is the identity convention in [F2]. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply $\epsilon$ and use $\epsilon(e_i)=w_i$ to obtain $Z_A(\Sigma_g)=\epsilon(H^g(\eta(1)))=\sum_i w_i^{1-g}$. The cylinder is $1_A$ by [F2], and for $g=1$ every summand is $1$, so the torus amplitude is $r$. [given, F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Sewing diagram

The arrows are the unit map, the $g$-fold handle operator, and the counit. Their composite is the scalar assigned to the closed surface; the diagram is a type-checked summary of the formula, not a proof premise.

```tikzcd
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\eta"] & A \arrow[r,"H^g"] & A \arrow[r,"\epsilon"] & \mathbb C
```

items.title: Positive weights characterize the specified Hermitian form
items.design_state: Assigned reserved design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded on the owning A/B page.
items.statement: For the semisimple closed model determined by the stated idempotent data, define $a^*=\sum_i\overline{a_i}e_i$ when $a=\sum_i a_i e_i$, and set $h(a,b)=\epsilon(a^*b)$. The form $h$ is a Hermitian positive-definite inner product exactly when every weight $w_i$ is a positive real number. The algebraic closed oriented TQFT exists for every nonzero complex weight; positivity is an additional condition for this specified Hilbert-space interpretation.

references.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories (short version)
Joachim Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D Topological Quantum Field Theories (Cambridge book excerpt)
Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3

items.strategy:
1.1 If $a=\sum_i a_i e_i$ and $b=\sum_i b_i e_i$, then $a^*b=\sum_i\overline{a_i}b_i e_i$, so $h(a,b)=\sum_i w_i\overline{a_i}b_i$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 If every $w_i$ is positive real, the formula in step 1.1 is Hermitian and $h(a,a)=\sum_i w_i|a_i|^2>0$ for each nonzero $a$, because at least one coefficient is nonzero. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Conversely, if $h$ is Hermitian and positive definite, then $w_i=h(e_i,e_i)$ is real by Hermitian symmetry and strictly positive by positive definiteness for every nonzero basis vector $e_i$. Thus all weights are positive real, proving the equivalence. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The classification used in [F2] assumes only the nonzero Frobenius weights, so the algebraic closed theory remains defined when the extra positivity condition fails; this separates the categorical model from the specified Hilbert-space interpretation. [given, F2, step 2.2] ∎

## Form matrix

For the basis $(e_i)$, the associated sesquilinear form has diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_r)$. Positivity is a property of this explicit matrix and does not follow from the existence of the oriented closed TQFT.

items.title: Nonsemisimple Frobenius sewing is also possible
items.design_state: Assigned reserved design item; complete current statement and argument are recorded on the owning A/B page.
items.statement: Let $A=\mathbb C[x]/(x^2)$ with basis $(1,x)$, unit $1$, multiplication inherited from the quotient, and Frobenius functional $\epsilon(1)=0$, $\epsilon(x)=1$. The bilinear pairing $b(a,b)=\epsilon(ab)$ has matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ in that basis, hence is nondegenerate. With the conjugate-linear involution fixing $x$, the form $h(a,b)=\epsilon(a^*b)$ is Hermitian but indefinite. Here a finite-dimensional algebra is semisimple when its Jacobson radical (the intersection of its maximal left ideals) is zero; $A$ is not semisimple because $x$ is a nonzero nilpotent in that radical. The closed oriented classification therefore gives a closed two-dimensional TQFT from a nonsemisimple Frobenius algebra without asserting positive reflection form data.

references.title: Joachim Kock, Frobenius algebras and 2D topological quantum field theories (short version)
Joachim Kock, Frobenius Algebras and 2D Topological Quantum Field Theories (Cambridge book excerpt)
Aaron D. Lauda and Hendryk Pfeiffer, Open-closed strings: Two-dimensional extended TQFTs and Frobenius algebras, arXiv:math/0510664v3

items.strategy:
1.1 Every class in $A$ is uniquely $a+bx$ with $a,b\in\mathbb C$, and $(a+bx)(c+dx)=ac+(ad+bc)x$ because $x^2=0$. This is the quotient of the associative commutative algebra $\mathbb C[x]$, so $A$ is a two-dimensional commutative unital associative algebra with nonzero nilpotent $x$. [given, algebra]

1.2 The pairing values are $b(1,1)=0$, $b(1,x)=1$, $b(x,1)=1$, and $b(x,x)=0$, so its matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and determinant $-1\ne0$. Hence $b$ is nondegenerate. [given, algebra]

2.1 Define $\Delta(1)=1\otimes x+x\otimes1$ and $\Delta(x)=x\otimes x$. On both basis elements, $(\epsilon\otimes1)\Delta=(1\otimes\epsilon)\Delta=\operatorname{id}_A$ as counit identities; the two coassociative composites on $1$ both equal $1\otimes x\otimes x+x\otimes1\otimes x+x\otimes x\otimes1$, and on $x$ both equal $x\otimes x\otimes x$. For the two Frobenius identities, bilinearity reduces to the four basis pairs $(1,1),(1,x),(x,1),(x,x)$; on these pairs all three composites $\Delta\mu$, $(1\otimes\mu)(\Delta\otimes1)$, and $(\mu\otimes1)(1\otimes\Delta)$ respectively equal $\Delta(1),\Delta(x),\Delta(x),0$. Thus the specified maps make $A$ a commutative Frobenius algebra. [given, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 The ideal $(x)$ is maximal because $A/(x)\cong\mathbb C$. For every maximal ideal $M$, the quotient $A/M$ is a field and the image of $x$ there is nilpotent because $x^2=0$; a field has no nonzero nilpotents, so $x\in M$. Hence $0\ne x\in J(A)$, the intersection of all maximal left ideals, and $A$ is not semisimple under the stated definition. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 For $a=a_0+a_1x$ and $b=b_0+b_1x$, $h(a,b)=\overline{a_0}b_1+\overline{a_1}b_0$, so $h(a,b)=\overline{h(b,a)}$ and the form is Hermitian. Also $h(1+x,1+x)=\epsilon((1+x)^2)=2$ while $h(1-x,1-x)=\epsilon((1-x)^2)=-2$, so it takes both signs and is not positive definite. [given, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By step 2.1 the algebra is finite-dimensional, commutative, and Frobenius, so [F1] applies over $k=\mathbb C$ and gives the closed oriented two-dimensional TQFT. This conclusion uses the closed category only and adds no open/closed or positivity claim. [given, F1, step 2.1] ∎
